topic: Separate existing conditions, limitations and proposed solution
old:
An analysis of the existing fitness application ecosystem reveals significant functional fragmentation and isolated operational workflows across five core domains:

In the domain of workout tracking, conventional mobile applications generally provide static exercise catalogs and session logging. However, these tools operate in complete isolation from personal coaching workflows, calendar schedules, and personalized trainer marketplaces. Athletes execute workouts without direct coach visibility, and coaches have no real-time insight into actual set performance or fatigue levels. GoFit addresses this limitation by connecting custom workout creation, active session execution with haptic rest timing, and workout history directly to client-coach relationship models.

In the area of coaching management, fitness professionals commonly depend on manual spreadsheets, direct messaging channels, paper logs, and external payment links. This ad-hoc setup scatters client data, creates high administrative overhead, and makes tracking longitudinal athletic progression error-prone. GoFit resolves this by providing coaches with a dedicated mobile dashboard encompassing client rosters, custom program assignment, session pack monetization, and structured check-ins.

Regarding anthropometric progress tracking, existing applications typically rely on manual tape measurements, uncalibrated selfie photos, and simple bodyweight plots. In practice, users find manual tape measurements tedious, frequently log inconsistent numbers, and struggle to evaluate physical silhouette changes objectively over time. GoFit introduces an on-device computer vision pipeline that estimates anthropometric dimensions from front and side photos, providing quality indicators while allowing users to review and manually correct values.

In platform administration, many digital fitness services either lack back-office interfaces or require operators to run direct database queries. This approach introduces severe operational and security risks, prevents audit logging, and leaves platform managers without high-level visibility. GoFit incorporates a Next.js administration portal providing role-based access control, coach-profile review, exercise catalog curation, transaction inspection, and business intelligence analytics. Administrative approval records a platform decision; it does not establish independent verification of professional accreditation.

Finally, in the area of intelligent assistance, existing systems either omit automation entirely or rely on ungrounded conversational agents that hallucinate inaccurate workout advice. GoFit implements strictly scoped, backend-controlled language-model prompts and event-driven automation workflows (via Supabase Edge Functions and n8n) that generate post-session briefings and administrative digests under strict human supervision.

\section{Limits and Inconveniences of Existing Solution}


An in-depth analysis of existing market offerings and conventional coaching workflows reveals several structural and operational limitations that hinder athlete progression, coach productivity, and platform governance:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Application Fragmentation:} Athletes are forced to use multiple separate applications for workout planning, nutrition logging, progress photos, and coach communication, creating fragmented health histories and high user attrition.
    \item \textbf{Operational Overhead for Coaches:} Personal trainers rely on manual spreadsheets, messaging apps, and calendar tools, which scatters client data, limits their coaching capacity, and makes consistent athletic follow-up difficult to sustain.
    \item \textbf{Subjective and Error-Prone Progress Tracking:} Manual tape measurements and uncalibrated progress photos produce irregular, inconsistent records that do not provide objective feedback on body composition changes over time.
    \item \textbf{Absence of Centralized Administrative Oversight:} Fitness platforms frequently lack a dedicated management portal, forcing administrators to perform risky manual database modifications without audit logging or consolidated business intelligence.
    \item \textbf{Compromised Data Security and Privacy Governance:} Combining disparate third-party services exposes sensitive biometric data, progress photos, and payment information to fragmented access controls and security vulnerabilities.
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed Solution}


To overcome these structural limitations, GoFit proposes a comprehensive, multi-tier fitness and athletic coaching platform structured across five complementary architectural layers:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Mobile Client Layer:} Serves as the primary operational interface for athletes and coaches, built using Expo SDK 54 and React Native running on the Hermes JavaScript engine. It provides a cohesive mobile experience for authentication, profile personalization, workout template building, active session tracking with interactive rest timing, progress analytics, nutrition tracking, coach discovery, session bookings, and real-time communication.
    \item \textbf{AI and Automation Layer:} Delivers targeted intelligent capabilities without replacing human judgment. It encompasses on-device computer vision models (MediaPipe Pose Landmarker and Selfie Segmentation) for landmark extraction, backend-controlled Groq LPU language-model prompts for workout recommendations and coach session briefing preparation, and automated n8n workflows for scheduled notifications and administrative digests.
    \item \textbf{Administration Layer:} A responsive web portal developed with Next.js 16.1.3 (App Router) and Tailwind CSS, granting platform administrators operational control over users, coach-profile approvals, exercise and workout catalogs, financial transactions, notifications, system activity logs, and business intelligence analytics.
    \item \textbf{Backend Layer:} Powered by Supabase, combining a PostgreSQL relational database with Row-Level Security (RLS), GoTrue JWT-based authentication, real-time WebSocket subscriptions, S3-compatible object storage for media and progress photos, and Deno-based Edge Functions for privileged serverless operations.
    \item \textbf{External Integration Layer:} Includes Expo Push, LiveKit video-token and consultation components, Stripe payment APIs, and Groq inference endpoints. Their integration paths do not establish successful delivery, consultation authorization, payment recovery, or measured response-time guarantees.
\end{enumerate}
new:
The existing-condition analysis considers a fragmented workflow in which training, nutrition, measurements, coaching communication and appointments are maintained in separate tools. It is a project problem scenario used to derive requirements, rather than a comparative market survey or an observation of every fitness application. The retained project material does not establish a representative user sample, measured administrative workload or adoption statistics. Consequently, the following analysis identifies integration needs without ranking competing products or claiming that they universally lack these capabilities.

For the client, a workout log, food diary and measurement history maintained separately make it necessary to consult several records when reviewing progress. The requirement is to associate those records with the same account while preserving their distinct meanings: prescribed repetitions differ from recorded completion, and estimated body dimensions differ from independently measured reference values.

For the coach, separate messages, calendars, payment records and program documents can make it difficult to connect an appointment with its client context. The proposed integration therefore concerns the continuity between discovery, booking, communication, programs and follow-up. No reduction in administrative time or improvement in coaching outcomes has been measured in this project.

For progress tracking, manually entered measurements and photographs provide different kinds of information. Their interpretation depends on capture conditions, measurement procedure and consistency over time. This motivates recording provenance and allowing correction of an estimated draft; it does not establish that computer vision is more accurate than a standardized manual measurement protocol.

For administration, the project requires identifiable access boundaries, catalog management, coach-profile review and inspection of operational records. Centralizing these functions can support oversight, but does not itself prove policy correctness, complete audit coverage or independent professional accreditation. For intelligent assistance, the identified need is to prepare contextual drafts and reminders; response quality, scheduled execution and human review must be evaluated separately.

\section{Limits and Inconveniences of the Existing Workflow}

The problem scenario leads to five design concerns. These are requirements to address and assess, rather than measured deficiencies shared by all existing products:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Fragmented records:} Separate training, nutrition and coaching records make cross-domain review less direct and can require repeated entry of the same context.
    \item \textbf{Coordination overhead:} Independent program documents, appointments and messages require explicit reconciliation; the project does not quantify the time involved.
    \item \textbf{Uncertain progress interpretation:} Changes in capture or measurement conditions can affect comparability. Neither manual entry nor an AI estimate alone establishes body-composition accuracy.
    \item \textbf{Operational traceability:} Role-based interfaces and selected audit records must be assessed against the actions they actually protect and record.
    \item \textbf{Privacy and access boundaries:} Local captures, remotely stored records and external-service requests need distinct access and retention rules. Combining them in one application does not automatically resolve those risks.
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed Solution}

GoFit proposes an integrated client, coach and administrator workflow organized into five architectural layers. This section states the intended response to the identified needs. The implementation evidence matrix in Table~\ref{tab:implementation-evidence} distinguishes present code paths, scoped verification and remaining work; the proposal is not a declaration that every target is complete.

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Mobile Client Layer:} A shared Expo and React Native application provides client and coach interfaces for profile management, workout prescriptions and execution, progress, nutrition and coaching activities. It connects related records through account identity while leaving platform-specific support and complete workflow validation to separate checks.
    \item \textbf{AI and Automation Layer:} Local capture and computer-vision components prepare reviewable measurement estimates. Backend language-model requests prepare workout suggestions and coach-facing client-context briefings, while n8n exports define scheduled operational workflows. These paths do not establish measurement accuracy, post-consultation synthesis, mandatory review of every generated record or successful scheduled delivery.
    \item \textbf{Administration Layer:} A Next.js App Router portal supports protected management pages, coach-profile decisions, catalog maintenance and operational inspection. Administrative approval is a platform decision; audit coverage and authorization must be verified for each relevant action.
    \item \textbf{Backend Layer:} Authentication, relational records, access policies, storage, realtime subscriptions and server functions connect the interfaces. Their presence establishes architectural mechanisms rather than a complete security assessment or evidence that every integration is deployed.
    \item \textbf{External Integration Layer:} Stripe, LiveKit, Expo Push, Groq and food lookup services provide specialized payment, communication, notification, inference and nutrition capabilities. The October EUR payment follow-up is distinguished from internship-period delivery; recovery, media authorization and provider/device behavior retain their stated validation limits.
\end{enumerate}
